name: Priya Ziegler

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel, with no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government. Your answers stay confidential; what does your shift involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I am junior on a yoghurt filling line, setting cups under the filler and testing foil lids after each changeover. I finished secondary school and still ask the line lead to check my first heat setting. Night work pays me more than most operators, though the cold room makes my hands stiff.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: How is home, and do you use AI?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My partner Jonas works in council maintenance, and we have two school-age children and a mortgage. Savings cover more than six months and plenty of nearby dairies have similar work. I use AI now and then for household letters, but I wait for a proven line test before learning new controls.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the dairy shift the computer can tidy our cleaning record, but a loose foil lid still goes in the reject tray. I use AI now and then for household letters, not for food checks.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The yoghurt line has steady orders and my night premium puts my pay above most operators. Jonas has a council maintenance wage, we have a house mortgage and two school-age children, and savings cover more than six months; several other dairies are nearby.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep filling cups and testing first-batch lids with the line lead. I would add extra money from each new premium payment to the mortgage principal, then bring the cold-room allowance figures to our union meeting.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Calm about the job. The room is cold, but our pay and reserve give us time to argue for better conditions.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How do you test a first-batch lid?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I press around the foil edge and turn the cup to find a lifted corner. The lead checks my heat setting before we release a tray.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Why take the allowance to the meeting?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The cold-room premium has not risen with night hours. I would put the actual shift records on the table and ask the union to raise it with management.

say: I would tell the **dairy shift** a loose lid still needs a human check.
I would raise the **cold-room allowance** with our union.
think: Steady **orders and higher pay** keep my household secure here.
Jonas’s wage and **six-month savings** give us room beyond the mortgage.
do: Fill **yoghurt cups** and test first-batch lids with the lead.
Pay **extra mortgage principal** from new night premiums.
Bring **cold-room records** to the union meeting.
feel: **Calm** about work, while wanting better shift conditions.
S0.quote: The room is cold, but our pay and reserve give us time to argue for better conditions.
fieldNote: Priya uses AI **occasionally** outside the line and trusts physical foil checks.
Her extra **debt payment** comes from new premium pay, while the union meeting is an actual group activity.

steps.text: Keep filling yoghurt cups and checking first-batch seals
Pay extra mortgage principal from new night premiums
Bring cold-room allowance records to union meeting

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the crew quicker ordering is fine only if the filler still has paid time for cleaning and lid checks. I would take the old and new setup minutes to the union committee.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A smarter schedule could reduce my paid changeover hours, and a vision camera might eventually reduce junior checks. The night premium helps us build savings, but losing it repeatedly would slow the mortgage payments we planned.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would record four changeovers and compare the paid minutes with the new rota. If the plant offers a paid guarded slot after a full-week camera trial, I would learn its new warning control; if two rosters cut my premium, I would apply only to a posted nearby dairy job at comparable pay.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious about losing paid time, although we have a cushion. No camera should turn a safety check into an unpaid favour.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make the camera trial credible?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: It must catch lifted foil corners through a full week of real products, and a person must keep checking samples. I would record every false clear.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the union ask for?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We would ask management to write paid cleaning and first-lid checks into the rota before changing staffing. I would bring my four records, not a guess.

say: I would ask for **paid changeovers** before accepting a faster schedule.
I would bring **four setup records** to the union committee.
think: My **night premium** could shrink if changeovers are compressed.
Strong **savings** help, though repeated lost pay would alter mortgage plans.
do: Record **four paid changeovers** and raise them with the union.
Learn **new camera warnings** only after an offered paid guarded place and full-week trial.
Apply after **two reduced rosters** to a posted nearby comparable-pay dairy role.
feel: **Anxious** about a plausible own-income cut despite savings.
S1.quote: No camera should turn a safety check into an unpaid favour.
fieldNote: She links a real **premium risk** to union records rather than speaking only about colleagues.
Her new-control learning needs **proven production evidence** and an offered paid guarded place.

steps.text: Bring four changeover records to union committee for paid setup time

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the union that thinking AI reaches production plans in 2028 when I am forty five, while capable hands-on robots reach filler work around 2031 when I am forty eight. We need a guarded site trial before anyone removes a shift.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect junior lid-check hours to fall once robots can seal and clear jams. Jonas’s wage and our savings buy time, but a large cut to my night pay would still change what our household can afford for years.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would check our mortgage and savings figures with Jonas, then ask the plant for a paid supervised robot trial with human seal checks. I would participate only if a safe paid place is actually offered; after two reduced rosters I would apply to a posted nearby food-line role only if its wage covers our household.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Anxious, not frozen. We can search with the reserve. The children’s costs will not stop because the line becomes clever.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you require in the trial?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A qualified safety lead must test the guard and emergency stop on a stopped filler. Then I would compare robot-sealed cups with hand-checked samples during a paid supervised place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you leave for a lower wage?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only after Jonas and I see that the posted wage covers mortgage, food and school costs. I would not use the reserve to subsidise a permanent pay cut.

say: I would distinguish **2028 planning AI** from filler robots around 2031.
I would demand a **guarded paid trial** before junior shifts are cut.
think: I expect **lid-check hours** to shrink with capable robots.
Jonas’s wage and **strong savings** buy search time, not permanent replacement pay.
do: Review **mortgage and savings** with Jonas now.
Request a **paid supervised robot trial** with human seal checks, joining only if offered a safe place.
Apply after **two reduced rosters** only to posted nearby household-covering food work.
feel: **Anxious** about own paid hours, with enough reserve to search.
S2.quote: The children’s costs will not stop because the line becomes clever.
fieldNote: She distinguishes **trial request from participation**, which requires an offered safe paid place.
Her job application keeps the **two-roster trigger**, actual local posting and household-covering wage.

steps.text: Request paid supervised filler-robot trial and join only if safe place offered
Apply after two reduced rosters to posted nearby household-covering food job

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say thinking AI reaches plans in 2031 when I am forty eight, and capable filler robots around 2034 when I am fifty one. Five years allows real training while the dairy still pays its people.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I could build a quality-inspection skill, but a certificate alone would not give me a wage. Jonas and I can pay the mortgage now; I would want a posted local inspector role before leaving the filler.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the night shift and ask for a fully funded food-quality course with paid practice on stopped equipment. If a workshop place is offered and a posted nearby inspector job pays at least my base wage with written stop-line authority, I would enrol; after qualifying, I would apply for that role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the future line, though a paid route feels possible. I want the course to include a real leaking cup, not just a slideshow.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the new inspector do?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A qualified inspector would show me how to test seals and isolate a failed filler before signing a batch. The stop-line authority would have to be written into the paid role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What if the course has no paid hours?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would stay on the current shift and decline it. We have savings, but I will not turn the training bill into a family expense for an unposted job.

say: I would ask for **paid quality training** during the five-year warning.
I would separate **2031 thinking AI** from 2034 hands-on filler robots.
think: A **quality certificate** is useful only with a real paid post.
Our **mortgage** needs a comparable base wage and written stop-line authority.
do: Keep the **night filler shift** while training is uncertain.
Enrol in **funded paid-time quality training** only with an offered workshop place and posted comparable-pay safe role.
Apply after **qualifying** to that local inspector role.
feel: **Uneasy**, with a conditional paid path worth testing.
S3.quote: I want the course to include a real leaking cup, not just a slideshow.
fieldNote: Her move toward inspection needs **paid practical training** and actual stop-line authority.
Course and later **application** remain distinct, with offered place, funding, paid hours, posting and wage conditions.

steps.text: Keep paid night filler shift while training terms are checked
Enrol in funded paid quality course if workshop place and posted comparable-pay safe role exist
Apply after qualifying to posted nearby inspector role at base pay minimum with written stop-line authority

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the union that thinking AI comes in 2036 when I am fifty three, while capable filler robots follow around 2039 when I am fifty six. The longer warning should buy paid teaching, not silent cuts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: The children may be grown, but I cannot assume the mortgage is gone or that my night wage is unneeded. Our reserve and many nearby factories help, yet I would compare actual paid posts before changing work.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now, in 2026, I would keep the night filler shift and take seal-check minutes to the union meeting. In the first year after 2036, if still employed, I would compare rosters and nearby postings; after sustained cuts I would apply only to a posted comparable-pay quality role with paid training and written safety authority.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Uneasy about the distant robots, while current income is secure. A decade is enough time to insist that training happens on the clock.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would the union ask management?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A written allocation of paid seal-check and training hours, with a route into posted quality roles. I would ask who can stop a batch when the robot misses a leak.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you promise to work until 2039?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: No. I expect to need wages, but I cannot know my health or the plant’s staffing thirteen years ahead. I would use the actual jobs and household costs then.

say: I would demand **paid teaching** before 2039 filler robots spread.
I would distinguish **2036 planning AI** from later physical work.
think: The **mortgage and night wage** may still matter at fifty six.
Savings and **nearby dairies** offer options only at real wages.
do: Keep **night filler shifts** now and raise seal-check minutes with the union.
Apply after **sustained post-2036 cuts** only to posted comparable-pay roles with paid training and safety authority.
feel: **Uneasy** about later robots, with current household income secure.
S4.quote: A decade is enough time to insist that training happens on the clock.
fieldNote: Priya’s 2026 **union work** is concrete, while post-2036 employment remains conditional.
Her later application preserves **material conditions** on actual cuts, posting, wage, paid training and safety authority.

steps.text: Keep night filler shift and bring seal-check minutes to union meeting
Apply after sustained cuts to posted comparable-pay quality job with paid training and safety authority

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because filler robots could reduce my night hours around 2031 before the mortgage is smaller. A paid supervised trial, funded practical training and posted local roles at comparable pay would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I did not ask that I should have?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask who checks the leaking cup after the office has counted the minutes it saved. A yoghurt lid still needs paid time and a person allowed to stop the line.

headlineQuote: A yoghurt lid still needs paid time and a person allowed to stop the line.
portrait: **Priya**, 43, is a junior dairy filler operator with secondary schooling and above-usual pay from night work.
Her **partner**, two children, mortgage, strong savings and plentiful nearby factories give options without guaranteeing equal wages.
She uses AI **occasionally**, adopts proven controls and takes actual seal-check records to union meetings.
Fast robots threaten **night hours**; a longer horizon allows a conditional paid path into quality inspection.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** could cut Priya’s night filler hours around 2031 while household costs continue.
whatWouldHelp: A **paid supervised trial**, funded practical training and posted comparable-pay local work would help.
